def kSmallestPairs(nums1, nums2, k):
    """translate this code from Visual Basic .NET to python:
```vb.net
Imports System
Imports System.Collections.Generic
Imports System.Linq

Module Program
    Sub Main(args As String())
        Dim nums1 As Integer() = {1, 7, 11}
        Dim nums2 As Integer() = {2, 4, 6}
        Dim k As Integer = 3
        Dim result As List(Of List(Of Integer)) = kSmallestPairs(nums1, nums2, k)
        Console.WriteLine("[{0}]", String.Join(",", result.Select(Function(inner) $"[{String.Join(",", inner)}]")))
        ' Output: [[1,2],[1,4],[1,6]]
    End Sub
    
    Public Function kSmallestPairs(nums1 As Integer(), nums2 As Integer(), k As Integer) As List(Of List(Of Integer))
        If nums1 Is Nothing OrElse nums2 Is Nothing Then
            Return New List(Of List(Of Integer))()
        End If
        
        Dim heap As New SortedSet(Of (Integer, Integer))()
        For i As Integer = 0 To Math.Min(k, nums1.Length) - 1
            heap.Add((nums1(i) + nums2(0), i))
        Next
        
        Dim result As New List(Of List(Of Integer))()
        While k > 0 AndAlso heap.Count > 0
            Dim (sum, i) As (Integer, Integer) = heap.Min
            heap.Remove((sum, i))
            Dim j As Integer = sum - nums1(i)
            result.Add(New List(Of Integer)() From {nums1(i), nums2(j)})
            If j + 1 < nums2.Length Then
                heap.Add((nums1(i) + nums2(j + 1), i))
            End If
            k -= 1
        End While
        
        Return result
    End Function
